The function \( f \) is defined as follows:
\[
f(n) = \left\{
\begin{array}{cl}
n + 10 & \text{if } n < 10, \\
f(n - 5) & \text{if } n \ge 10.
\end{array}
\right.
\]

To find the maximum value of \( f(n) \), we analyze the function for different values of \( n \).

For \( n < 10 \), the function is \( f(n) = n + 10 \). The maximum value in this range occurs at \( n = 9 \), giving \( f(9) = 9 + 10 = 19 \).

For \( n \ge 10 \), the function is defined recursively as \( f(n) = f(n - 5) \). This means we need to evaluate \( f \) at \( n - 5 \) repeatedly until we reach a value less than 10. 

By examining values of \( n \ge 10 \):
- \( f(10) = f(5) = 15 \)
- \( f(11) = f(6) = 16 \)
- \( f(12) = f(7) = 17 \)
- \( f(13) = f(8) = 18 \)
- \( f(14) = f(9) = 19 \)

For \( n \ge 15 \), the values of \( f(n) \) repeat the sequence 15, 16, 17, 18, 19. Thus, the maximum value in this repeating cycle is 19.

Therefore, the maximum value of the function \( f(n) \) is \(\boxed{19}\).
